title: Client Policy Compositional Engine — API & Config Notes
body:
Context: quick brain dump of a lightweight client-side policy engine (CPE) API to let edge clients compose runtime safety, routing, and feature-gating decisions before sending calls to Redwood. Purpose is to push cheap checks and routing decisions into client runtime to reduce server-side cost and allow tenant-specific overrides without a full private-deploy control plane change.

Non-goals: not trying to replace PDP/PIP for enterprise policy. This lives as an optional client lib+small JSON config that runtime integrators can opt into.

High-level goals:
- Compositional: allow multiple policy fragments (built-in, tenant, feature, experiment) to be merged with deterministic precedence rules.
- Lightweight: config ~ few KB, evaluate under 1ms on typical mobile CPU.
- Observable: emit small telemetry events (decision id, matched rules) with sampling.
- Safe defaults: deny-by-default for unknown/unsafe actions; explicit allow for simple passthrough flows.

Basic concepts and primitives:
- policy fragment: small JSON with rules + metadata + version
- predicate: small expression evaluated against request context (strings, enums, existence, numeric ranges)
- effect: allow | deny | route:VARIANT | annotate:{k:v}
- composition: ordering + merging rules (higher priority fragments win; annotations merge)

Example fragment (textual; kept intentionally simple):

FRAGMENT: tenant-safety-v1
{
  "id": "tenant-safety-v1",
  "priority": 50,
  "predicates": [
    {"id":"contains-pii","expr":"request.text contains /SSN|credit card|PII/i"}
  ],
  "rules": [
    {"pred":"contains-pii","effect":"deny","reason":"tenant-blocked-pii"}
  ],
  "meta": {"author":"infra-safety","created":"2024-09-18"}
}

FRAGMENT: stale-experiment-allow
{
  "id": "exp-allow-xyz",
  "priority": 10,
  "rules": [
    {"pred":"true","effect":"route:small-quant"}
  ],
  "meta": {"note":"temporary experiment routing override"}
}

Evaluation model (procedural):
1) Gather fragments: builtins (priority 0), tenant (50), feature flags (40), local overrides (60).
2) Sort descending by numeric priority.
3) For each fragment in order, evaluate predicates; if a rule matches, apply effect.
   - allow/deny is terminal (stop) unless rule has "continue:true" flag
   - route:* is terminal and returns a chosen model-variant token to client routing layer
   - annotate adds to a merged annotation dict (non-terminal)
4) If no fragment matches, fallback: built-in-default (allow + route:default) OR explicit deny depending on config mode.

Config schema (compact BNF-like):
- fragment := {id, priority:int, predicates:[], rules:[], meta:{}}
- predicate := {id, expr:string}  // expr is small grammar (see below)
- rule := {pred:id|"true", effect:string, continue?:bool, ttl?:int}

Predicate expression grammar (intent, simple subset for fast eval):
- terms: identifier (request.xxx), string literals, numeric literals, regex literals (/.../i)
- ops: contains, ==, !=, <, >, in (list), exists
- connectors: and, or, not, parentheses for grouping
- example: (request.lang == "en" and exists(request.user.email)) or (request.text contains /refund|chargeback/i)

Runtime API shape (client-side library surface):
- init(configFragments: [fragment], options?) -> handle
- evaluate(handle, requestContext) -> DecisionResult
- DecisionResult: {decision_id, outcome: allow|deny|route, route_variant?:string, annotations:{}, matched_fragments:[id], telemetry_hint?:string}

Example JS pseudo: 
const handle = CPE.init({fragments: [builtins, tenant, featureFlags], mode: "fail-closed"});
const res = handle.evaluate({text: userPrompt, user: {id:123, tier:"free"}, lang: "en"});
if (res.outcome === 'deny') { showModal('We cannot process that request'); }
else if (res.outcome === 'route') { router.callModel(res.route_variant, ...); }

Composition subtleties and open decisions (notes to self):
- Annotation merging semantics: prefer longest-prefix keys? Use list-of-values? For now keep map of arrays: {k: [v1,v2]} so we can blame sources.
- "continue" semantics: default terminal for allow/deny/routes. Allow explicit continue:true when fragment is an "assertion" fragment (e.g., add annotations but keep evaluating).
- Priority tie-breaker: deterministic tie-break by fragment id lexicographic order. Document that.
- Performance: parse regexes once at init; compile simple predicate AST into bytecode-ish evaluation. Need microbench on Android 2019 device.
- Security: fragment configs can ship from tenant control plane; must be signed or have nonce+version to prevent client override injection.

Telemetry plan (minimal):
- emit sampling event when evaluate() runs: {decision_id, matched_fragments, outcome, eval_ms}
- sample rate default 0.1% on mobile, 1% on desktop, configurable via runtime options (not fragment-level to avoid info leak).
- DO NOT include request text in telemetry unless explicitly opted-in and redacted. Include hashed request fingerprint instead.

Edge-router integration:
- DecisionResult.route_variant should map to Redwood routing token (e.g., "small-quant" -> router will prefer quantized model group).
- Client should attach decision_id and matched_fragments header: "X-CPE-Decisions: id=...,frags=tenant-safety-v1,exp-allow-xyz" for downstream audit and optional server-side enforcement check.

Example ascii diagram (sequence):
Client app -> CPE.evaluate(request) -> DecisionResult -> if route -> Router picks variant -> call backend with X-CPE-Decisions header

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we prevent tenant fragments from silently escalating priority to override safety builtins? Options: immutable builtins with mandatory higher priority, or signed override tokens for tenant fragments.
- Default "mode": fail-open vs fail-closed. Recommend configurable at init + per-tenant policy (e.g., enterprise strongly prefers fail-closed).
- Migration story: provide server-side evaluation as a reference, then enable client-side caching of fragments and a signed delta update mechanism.
- UX: how to surface deny reasons to users without leaking policy internals? Map internal reasons to canned user-facing messages in client locale.

Notes from pairing w/ Ethan (2025-01-24):
- Ethan: keep predicate grammar intentionally tiny to avoid accidental complexity. Regex allowed but discouraged; provide common predicates for PII detection that run fast.
- Maya: suggested adding a "confidence" field to rules so experiments can mark non-blocking soft-deny that surfaces a warning rather than outright deny.

Rough implementation tasks:
- [ ] spec: finalize predicate grammar + evaluation semantics (PRI-1)
- [ ] lib: JS + mobile Kotlin/Swift prototypes
- [ ] infra: signed fragment delivery API + simple webhook for immediate push
- [ ] infra: server-side enforcement mirror for auditing
- [ ] perf: microbench suite, mobile targets

Grainy example: final merged decision (stringified for audit):
{
  "decision_id": "cpe::20250124::a1b2c3",
  "outcome": "route",
  "route_variant": "small-quant",
  "annotations": {"safety_checks": ["tenant-safety-v1:deny-blocked"], "exp": ["exp-allow-xyz"]},
  "matched_fragments": ["tenant-safety-v1","exp-allow-xyz"]
}

Last notes: keep this in users/ because it's a personal design draft. Need to sync with infra-safety and product-hosted-api before elevating to shared spec.

--- end of scratchpad ---
